narrative: The model estimated a 58.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That is above the bank’s decision threshold, so your loan was denied. The strongest reason was the size of the loan you requested: 13,756 DM, far above the average approved request of about 3,020 DM. This was the top factor and pushed the decision toward bad credit. The second most important factor was your checking-account status; having no checking account was not treated as a negative by the model and actually counted in your favor. The third most important factor was your savings information; having unknown or no savings was also treated as a favorable factor in the model’s ranking, not as the main reason for denial. In other words, two of the three largest factors worked in your favor, but the unusually large requested amount outweighed them and led to the denial. To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a substantially smaller loan, ask the lender what amount would fit their risk limits, and provide strong documentation of income and ability to repay. If possible, add a guarantor or collateral and correct any missing account or savings information before reapplying.
